**35 xfail тестов** — все ожидаемо проваливаются. Вот полная картина по модулям:

---

## `normalise_job_rows` — 8 тестов

| Тест | Причина падения |
|------|----------------|
| `test_parse_salary_k_suffix` | `parse_salary("£50K per Annum")` → `int("50K per Annum")` → `ValueError` |
| `test_parse_salary_range_with_k` | `parse_salary("1K - 3K per Annum")` → та же ошибка |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[£31K per Annum]` | K-суффикс, другая сумма |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[2 - 3 per Annum]` | Диапазон без £ и K |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[15 - 17 per Annum]` | Диапазон без символов |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[$2 per Annum]` | Доллар вместо фунта |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[00-14]` | Дефисный формат без смысла |
| `test_normalise_missing_scraped_has_sli_entry` | `except Exception: pass` — строка теряется молча, в SLI-лог ничего не попадает |

**Корень:** `parse_salary` делает `int(str(value).replace("£","").replace(",",""))` — не обрабатывает суффиксы, диапазоны и чужие символы.

---

## `drop_duplicate_jobs` — 1 тест

| Тест | Причина падения |
|------|----------------|
| `test_dedup_different_job_ids_same_title_company_both_kept` | Ключ `title\|company` — две разные вакансии в разных городах с одинаковым тайтлом и компанией сливаются в одну |

**Корень:** `dedupe_key` должен использовать `job_id`, а не `title|company`.

---

## `resolve_job_town` — 11 тестов

| Тест | Причина падения |
|------|----------------|
| `test_resolve_location_with_country_suffix` | `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` → `lookup_town` ищет точное совпадение, суффикс не отрезается (555 вакансий) |
| `test_resolve_location_with_gb_suffix` | `"Bolton, GB"` — то же, code-суффикс (12 вакансий) |
| `test_resolve_crewe_not_in_towns` | `"Crewe"` — город есть в реальности, нет в словаре `TOWNS` |
| `test_resolve_location_placeholder_fallback` | `"2 Locations"` — placeholder, `structured_job.locations` никогда не проверяется (337 вакансий) |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Derby, Derbyshire, ...]` | Трёхчастный формат: суффикс + регион не отрезаются |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Chester, Cheshire, ...]` | То же |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Bradford, West Yorkshire, ...]` | То же |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Birmingham, Warwickshire, ...]` | То же |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Glasgow, Glasgow City, ...]` | То же |
| `test_resolve_hybrid_remote_formats[Hybrid - 2 days Warrington]` | Embedded-город не извлекается из hybrid-строки |
| `test_resolve_hybrid_remote_formats[Remote - UK]` | Remote-тип локации вообще не обрабатывается |

**Корень:** `lookup_town` делает только `TOWNS.get(text.strip().lower())` — один exact-match без парсинга формата.

---

## `match_jobs` — 14 тестов

| Тест | Причина падения |
|------|----------------|
| `test_matched_titles_case_insensitive` | `"controls engineer" in "Controls Engineer"` → `False` |
| `test_matched_titles_lowercase_profile_title` | `"cnc miller" in "CNC Miller"` → `False` |
| `test_matched_titles_non_adjacent_words` | `"Quality Engineer" in "Quality and Warranty Engineer"` → `False` |
| `test_matched_titles_case_real_feed[Business Development Manager]` | Профиль: `"business development manager"`, фид: `"Business Development Manager"` |
| `test_matched_titles_case_real_feed[Business Development Manager - North]` | То же + суффикс |
| `test_matched_titles_case_real_feed[CNC Turner Setter/Programmer ...]` | Профиль: `"cnc turner"`, фид: `"CNC Turner Setter/..."` |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Engineer - Electrical ...]` | Слова `"Electrical"` и `"Engineer"` есть, но не рядом |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Sr. Applications Engineer - Electrical]` | То же |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[PSV / HGV Engineer ... / Electrical Engineer]` | То же |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[PSV / HGV Engineer ... / Mechanical Engineer]` | То же |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Manufacturing Services Technician ...]` | `"Manufacturing Technician"` — слова не рядом |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Principal Engineer - Product Safety]` | `"Product Engineer"` — слова не рядом |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Highways Engineer – Design ...]` | `"Design Engineer"` — слова не рядом |
| `test_match_jobs_company_legal_suffix_stripped` | `"Cobalt Zephyr Holdings"` ≠ `"Cobalt Zephyr"` — точное строковое сравнение |

**Корень:** `matched_titles` делает `t in job_title` — регистрозависимый substring, а нужна проверка «все слова профиля присутствуют в тайтле вакансии в любом порядке».

---

## `test_labelled_sample` — 1 тест

| Тест | Причина падения |
|------|----------------|
| `test_v1_pipeline_recall_above_50_percent` | v1 находит **0 из 11** YES-вакансий: 10 отклонены в `resolve_job_town` (UNKNOWN_LOCATION), 1 (J685745) — в `match_jobs` (NO_TITLE_MATCH). Recall = 0% < 50%. |

---

Когда v2 чинит баг, соответствующие xfail переходят в `XPASS` и ломают CI — это и есть спека.

content.content:
1	# Notes
2	
3	## LLM Provider
4	
5	[Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/jev) is a good fit here — the task is essentially data comparison, so the most important thing is normalizing the data correctly.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Architecture
10	
11	### How the runtime builds the recruiter profile
12	
13	`load_search_inputs()` in [worker_runtime.py](v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py) reads the `profile_a/` directory and **merges three files into one dict**:
14	
15	```python
16	{
17	  "profile_id": "a",
18	  "companies":  [{"name": "Aire Calder", "industry": null}, ...],  # from company_searches.json
19	  "titles":     ["Controls Engineer", "Mechanical Engineer", ...],  # from job_title_searches.json
20	  "locations":  [{"name": "Warrington", "type": "sub_region", ...}, ...]  # from location_searches.json
21	}
22	```
23	
24	This dict becomes `context["profile"]` and travels through the entire pipeline.
25	
26	### Job structure in `jobs_raw.jsonl`
27	
28	Each line looks like:
29	
30	```json
31	{
32	  "job_id": "J123456",
33	  "scraped": {
34	    "title":    "Controls Engineer",
35	    "company":  "Aire Calder",
36	    "location": "Warrington",
37	    "salary":   "£45,000"
38	  },
39	  "source_url": "...",
40	  "page": {
41	    "http_status": 200,
42	    "title_tag":   "Controls Engineer | Aire Calder",
43	    "h1":          "Controls Engineer",
44	    "meta":        {},
45	    "visible_text": "...",
46	    "structured_job": {
47	      "title":     "Controls Engineer",
48	      "company":   "Aire Calder",
49	      "locations": ["Warrington"]
50	    }
51	  }
52	}
53	```
54	
55	`scraped.*` — what the scraper extracted from markup (often truncated, empty, or wrong).
56	`page.*` — the raw page fetched once: HTTP status plus all visible fields.
57	
58	### Pipeline flow
59	
60	```
61	jobs_raw.jsonl
62	    │
63	    ▼ load_job_feed
64	    │  → reads line by line; row["page"] and row["scraped"] available
65	    │
66	    ▼ normalise_job_rows
67	    │  → picks only scraped.{title, company, location, salary}
68	    │  → page is kept as-is in row["page"]
69	    │
70	    ▼ drop_duplicate_jobs
71	    │  → dedup by key title|company
72	    │
73	    ▼ resolve_job_town
74	    │  → takes row["location"] from scraped, looks it up in TOWNS dict
75	    │  → adds: row["town"], row["region"], row["country"]
76	    │
77	    ▼ match_jobs   ← profile_a files meet jobs here
78	    │
79	    │  [company check]   row["company"] ∈ {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}?
80	    │  [title check]     any t in profile["titles"] is a substring of row["title"]?
81	    │  [location check]  row["town"] ∈ towns_covered(loc) for any loc in profile["locations"]?
82	    │
83	    ▼ portal_matches_output
84	       → writes runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl
85	```
86	
87	---
88	
89	## Known Bugs in v1
90	
91	### 1. No dead-link filter (critical)
92	
93	The spec says HTTP 404 and 410 must always be rejected. v1 has no such module.
94	
95	| Status    | Count | Note                           |
96	| --------- | ----- | ------------------------------ |
97	| HTTP 200  | 868   | live                           |
98	| HTTP 403  | 455   | blocked (live, scraper failed) |
99	| HTTP 404  | 46    | should be rejected             |
100	| HTTP 410  | 129   | should be rejected             |
101	| HTTP 405  | 3     | live (method not supported)    |
102	| HTTP None | 10    | no page at all                 |
103	
104	8 of 49 "no" labels in `labelled_sample` are 404/410 jobs — they currently pass through to `match_jobs`.
105	
106	---
107	
108	### 2. `resolve_job_town` drops 10 of 11 correct answers
109	
110	Checked all "yes" jobs from `labelled_sample` against the TOWNS dict:
111	
112	| job_id  | scraped.location             | Passes?         |
113	| ------- | ---------------------------- | --------------- |
114	| J685745 | "Runcorn"                    | ✓ only one     |
115	| J849031 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |
116	| J442509 | "Crewe"                      | ✗ not in TOWNS |
117	| J576140 | "2 Locations"                | ✗              |
118	| J858474 | "Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"   | ✗              |
119	| J355784 | "Bangor Bus Depot"           | ✗              |
120	| J936283 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |
121	
122	Root causes:
123	
124	- **Country suffix**: `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` — need to strip `, United Kingdom`
125	- **Unknown cities**: `"Crewe"`, `"Knutsford"` — present in profile `includes`, missing from TOWNS
126	- **Placeholders**: `"2 Locations"`, `"10 Locations"` — must fall back to `structured_job.locations`
127	- **Addresses**: `"Bangor Bus Depot"`, `"Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"` — need city extraction
128	- **Empty location**: 420 jobs have no location — all silently lost
129	
130	---
131	
132	### 3. `scraped.title` contains abbreviations and truncations
133	
134	The scraper frequently stores garbage instead of the real title:
135	
136	| scraped.title | structured_job / title_tag                   |
137	| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
138	| "HC engineer" | "HV Commissioning Engineer"                  |
139	| "MD engineer" | "Mechanical Design Engineer"                 |
140	| "SC systems"  | "Software & Control Systems Engineers"       |
141	| "SM manager"  | "Senior Marketing Manager - Financial Lines" |
142	
143	`match_jobs` compares against `row["title"]` which comes from `scraped.title`. The real title is in `page.title_tag` or `page.structured_job.title` — matching must use those.
144	
145	---
146	
147	### 4. `matched_titles` — substring instead of word-by-word matching
148	
149	```python
150	# v1: substring containment
151	return [t for t in titles if t in job_title]
152	```
153	
154	Spec requires: *"every word of the profile title appears in the job's real title in any order, ignoring case, punctuation & a trailing plural s"*.
155	
156	What breaks with substring:
157	
158	- `"cnc miller" in "CNC Miller"` → `False` (case-sensitive)
159	- `"Quality Engineer" in "Quality and Warranty Engineer"` → `False` (words not adjacent)
160	- `"Controls Engineer" in "Senior Controls Engineer"` → `True` — works by coincidence
161	
162	From labelled data: job `J602066` has title `"Quality and Warranty Engineer"` and should match profile title `"Quality Engineer"` (both words present), but substring check returns `False`.
163	
164	---
165	
166	### 5. Company matching — exact equality against `scraped.company` only
167	
168	```python
169	# v1
170	if row["company"] not in companies:  # exact string from scraped.company
171	    reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
172	```
173	
174	Problems:
175	
176	- `scraped.company` often contains a different company than what's on the page (e.g. `scraped="Viaduct Thornbury Systems"` vs `structured_job.company="Delta North Granary"`)
177	- Profile names include legal suffixes (`Ltd`, `ENGINEERING LTD`, `The Group`, `Holdings`, `UK`) that may differ from scraped data — spec requires fuzzy matching ignoring those suffixes
178	
179	From labelled data: `J809819` — `scraped.company = "Cobalt Zephyr Holdings"`, profile contains `"Cobalt Zephyr"` → should match, but doesn't due to the `Holdings` suffix.
180	
181	Spec also requires checking the company name **across the whole page** (title_tag, h1, URL, visible_text, structured_job) — pipeline only looks at `scraped.company`.
182	
183	---
184	
185	### 6. Remote location type not implemented
186	
187	Profile contains:
188	
189	```json
190	{"name": "Remote (UK)", "type": "remote", "includes": ["Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"]}
191	```
192	
193	`towns_covered()` returns `{"Remote (UK)", "Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"}`, but `row["town"]` comes from the TOWNS dict which contains none of these values. Remote jobs never match.
194	
195	Spec: remote = jobs where the employer explicitly states remote/home-based in that country — must check `visible_text` and `structured_job.locations`.
196	
197	---
198	
199	### 7. `structured_job.locations` is never used
200	
201	135 jobs have `structured_job.locations` — a list of strings like `["Birmingham, GB"]`, `["manchester, Lancashire, United Kingdom"]`, `["United Kingdom", "Remote"]`. This is the most reliable location source, but the pipeline ignores it entirely.
202	
203	---
204	
205	### 8. `normalise_job_rows` — silent error swallowing
206	
207	```python
208	try:
209	    scraped = raw["scraped"]
210	    rows.append({...})
211	except Exception:
212	    pass  # row silently lost — no rejection reason, no SLI entry
213	```
214	
215	---
216	
217	### 9. `parse_salary` crashes on real data
218	
219	Values in the feed: `"£50K per Annum"`, `"1K - 3K per Annum"`, `"$2 per Annum"` — all cause `ValueError` inside `int(...)`. Not critical (only 12 jobs have salary), but combined with the `except Exception: pass` above, rows are silently lost.
220	
221	---
222	
223	### 10. Dedup by `title|company` instead of `job_id`
224	
225	[drop_duplicate_jobs.py:18](v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/drop_duplicate_jobs.py#L18): key `f"{row['title']}|{row['company']}"`.
226	
227	Two different jobs at the same company with the same title in different cities will be incorrectly merged. The correct key is `job_id`.
228	
229	## Data Analysis — data/ (excluding golden)
230	
231	### 1. jobs_raw.jsonl — 1,529 jobs
232	
233	HTTP status breakdown:
234	
235	| Status        | Count | %     |
236	| ------------- | ----- | ----- |
237	| 200 OK        | 868   | 56.8% |
238	| 403 Forbidden | 455   | 29.8% |
239	| 410 Gone      | 129   | 8.4%  |
240	| 404 Not Found | 46    | 3.0%  |
241	| Other / empty | 31    | 2.0%  |
242	
243	43% of jobs are inaccessible. Of those, 11.4% are dead links (404/410) that should be filtered.
244	
245	Field fill rates:
246	
247	| Field               | Filled                       |
248	| ------------------- | ---------------------------- |
249	| scraped.title       | 100%                         |
250	| scraped.company     | 100%                         |
251	| scraped.location    | 72.5% (420 missing)          |
252	| scraped.salary      | 0.8% (12 of 1,529)           |
253	| page.title_tag      | 39.8%                        |
254	| page.meta           | 38.8%                        |
255	| page.structured_job | 27.1%                        |
256	| page.h1             | 16.0%                        |
257	| page.visible_text   | 0% (empty in entire dataset) |
258	
259	**Critical finding:** `visible_text` is completely empty across the whole dataset. The company-matching rule from OUTPUT_FORMAT.json (search across page body text) cannot be applied — there is no data to search.
260	
261	### 2. Location signals
262	
263	- Unique location strings: 340
264	- 212 jobs have `"2 Locations"`, 46 have `"3 Locations"`, etc. — these are not parsed
265	- Top real locations: London (37), Derby (32), Bristol (24), Glasgow (17)
266	- Matches against profile cities (naive search): 164 / 1,529 (10.7%)
267	
268	### 3. Title signals (word-level matching)
269	
270	- Unique job titles: 1,348
271	- Matches against profile (all words present in title): 118 / 1,529 (7.7%)
272	- Top matched profile titles: Controls Engineer (24), Electrical Engineer (12), Design Engineer (10), Operations Manager (9), Maintenance Technician (9)
273	
274	### 4. Company signals
275	
276	- Profile companies: 408 (199 with industry specified)
277	- Company matches (normalised): 1,049 / 1,529 (68.6%)
278	- High match rate because the entire feed appears to have been generated from the same company list.
279	
280	### 5. Signal intersection
281	
282	| Condition                              | Jobs          |
283	| -------------------------------------- | ------------- |
284	| Company only                           | 1,049 (68.6%) |
285	| Title only                             | 118 (7.7%)    |
286	| Location only                          | 164 (10.7%)   |
287	| All three (company + title + location) | 35 (2.3%)     |
288	
289	### 6. labelled_sample.jsonl — 60 labelled jobs
290	
291	- yes (match): 11 (18.3%)
292	- no: 49 (81.7%)
293	
294	All 60 job_ids are present in jobs_raw.jsonl. Of the 11 positives, only 9 have `matched_company` / `matched_location` / `matched_job_title` filled; 2 have those fields empty despite `decision=yes` — an annotation anomaly.
295	
296	---
297	
298	## Data investigation: run `20261020T153054` vs `profile_a` inputs
299	
300	### Pipeline funnel — where jobs are lost
301	
302	```
303	load_job_feed        1529  →  pass: 1529 (100%)
304	drop_duplicates      1517  →  pass: 1445 (95.3%)  | rejected: 72 DUPLICATE
305	resolve_job_town     1445  →  pass:     6 (0.4%)  | rejected: 1439 UNKNOWN_LOCATION  ← BOTTLENECK
306	match_jobs              6  →  pass:     2 (33.3%) | rejected: 3 COMPANY_NOT_LISTED, 1 NO_TITLE_MATCH
307	OUTPUT                  2 jobs
308	```
309	
310	### Signal correlation with the dataset
311	
312	| Dimension                                           | Matches           | % of 1,529 |
313	| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------- |
314	| Company (exact match)                               | **1,021**   | 66.8%      |
315	| Location (token match against towns)                | **136**     | 8.9%       |
316	| Title (word-match against profile)                  | ~**160**    | ~10.5%     |
317	| **Triple intersection (manual analysis)**     | **56**      | 3.7%       |
318	| Of which false-geo (Liverpool NSW, Warrington PA…) | −6               |            |
319	| **Real UK jobs that should match**            | **~48–50** |            |
320	| **Worker found**                              | **2**       | 0.13%      |
321	
322	### Root cause: `resolve_job_town` only handles bare-city lookup
323	
324	Location format breakdown in the dataset:
325	
326	| Format                           | Count       | Worker handling              |
327	| -------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
328	| `"City, United Kingdom"`       | 567 (37%)   | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |
329	| Bare city (1–2 words)           | 459 (30%)   | ✅ only if in hardcoded dict |
330	| Empty string                     | 420 (27.5%) | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |
331	| `"Hybrid - 2 days Warrington"` | 1 (0.1%)    | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |
332	| US/AU false positives            | 15 (1%)     | needs country filter         |
333	
334	Of the 567 jobs with `"City, United Kingdom"` format — **80 have a city from the profile** (Manchester, Birmingham, Liverpool, etc.) and all are lost because the resolver cannot strip the `, United Kingdom` suffix.
335	
336	### The 6 jobs that passed the resolver
337	
338	Only jobs with a **bare city name** (`Wrexham`, `Chester`, `Runcorn`) hit the hardcoded TOWNS dict. Of those:
339	
340	- **2 passed** (Inkwell Copperleaf Group — present in companies list, Wrexham → North Wales)
341	- **3 rejected** at COMPANY_NOT_LISTED (`Mersey Ironbridge`, `Moorside Millrace` — not in the list)
342	- **1 rejected** at NO_TITLE_MATCH (`Software Engineer III, Digital Pathology…` — `systems engineer` is too weak a match)
343	
344	### Top missed patterns (54 missed of 56)
345	
346	53 of 54 are blocked at `resolve_job_town`. Main patterns:
347	
348	- `"Bolton, GB"` — 5 Controls Engineer jobs @ Aire Calder / Aire Northwind / Ancoats Castlefield
349	- `"Manchester, United Kingdom"` — 4 jobs
350	- `"Liverpool, United Kingdom"` — 4 jobs
351	- `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` — 6 jobs
352	- `"Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"` — 3 jobs at Lowther Brindley
353	- `"Wolverhampton, United Kingdom"` — 2 jobs
354	
355	### Conclusion
356	
357	The worker **works** — architecture and contracts are correct. But `resolve_job_town` is an intentionally broken module (noted in CLAUDE.md): it uses exact-match against a tiny hardcoded dict, whereas the real requirement is parsing multi-format location strings. Fixing this module alone would raise output from 2 to ~48 jobs (~24×).
358	
359	## `normalise_job_rows` — 8 тестов
360	
361	| Тест                                                   | Причина падения                                                                                            |
362	| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
363	| `test_parse_salary_k_suffix`                             | `parse_salary("£50K per Annum")` → `int("50K per Annum")` → `ValueError`                                        |
364	| `test_parse_salary_range_with_k`                         | `parse_salary("1K - 3K per Annum")` → та же ошибка                                                          |
365	| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[£31K per Annum]`   | K-суффикс, другая сумма                                                                                |

# Notes

## LLM Provider

[Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/jev) is a good fit here — the task is essentially data comparison, so the most important thing is normalizing the data correctly.

---

## Architecture

### How the runtime builds the recruiter profile

`load_search_inputs()` in [worker_runtime.py](v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py) reads the `profile_a/` directory and **merges three files into one dict**:

```python
{
  "profile_id": "a",
  "companies":  [{"name": "Aire Calder", "industry": null}, ...],  # from company_searches.json
  "titles":     ["Controls Engineer", "Mechanical Engineer", ...],  # from job_title_searches.json
  "locations":  [{"name": "Warrington", "type": "sub_region", ...}, ...]  # from location_searches.json
}
```

This dict becomes `context["profile"]` and travels through the entire pipeline.

### Job structure in `jobs_raw.jsonl`

Each line looks like:

```json
{
  "job_id": "J123456",
  "scraped": {
    "title":    "Controls Engineer",
    "company":  "Aire Calder",
    "location": "Warrington",
    "salary":   "£45,000"
  },
  "source_url": "...",
  "page": {
    "http_status": 200,
    "title_tag":   "Controls Engineer | Aire Calder",
    "h1":          "Controls Engineer",
    "meta":        {},
    "visible_text": "...",
    "structured_job": {
      "title":     "Controls Engineer",
      "company":   "Aire Calder",
      "locations": ["Warrington"]
    }
  }
}
```

`scraped.*` — what the scraper extracted from markup (often truncated, empty, or wrong).
`page.*` — the raw page fetched once: HTTP status plus all visible fields.

### Pipeline flow

```
jobs_raw.jsonl
    │
    ▼ load_job_feed
    │  → reads line by line; row["page"] and row["scraped"] available
    │
    ▼ normalise_job_rows
    │  → picks only scraped.{title, company, location, salary}
    │  → page is kept as-is in row["page"]
    │
    ▼ drop_duplicate_jobs
    │  → dedup by key title|company
    │
    ▼ resolve_job_town
    │  → takes row["location"] from scraped, looks it up in TOWNS dict
    │  → adds: row["town"], row["region"], row["country"]
    │
    ▼ match_jobs   ← profile_a files meet jobs here
    │
    │  [company check]   row["company"] ∈ {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}?
    │  [title check]     any t in profile["titles"] is a substring of row["title"]?
    │  [location check]  row["town"] ∈ towns_covered(loc) for any loc in profile["locations"]?
    │
    ▼ portal_matches_output
       → writes runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl
```

---

## Known Bugs in v1

### 1. No dead-link filter (critical)

The spec says HTTP 404 and 410 must always be rejected. v1 has no such module.

| Status    | Count | Note                           |
| --------- | ----- | ------------------------------ |
| HTTP 200  | 868   | live                           |
| HTTP 403  | 455   | blocked (live, scraper failed) |
| HTTP 404  | 46    | should be rejected             |
| HTTP 410  | 129   | should be rejected             |
| HTTP 405  | 3     | live (method not supported)    |
| HTTP None | 10    | no page at all                 |

8 of 49 "no" labels in `labelled_sample` are 404/410 jobs — they currently pass through to `match_jobs`.

---

### 2. `resolve_job_town` drops 10 of 11 correct answers

Checked all "yes" jobs from `labelled_sample` against the TOWNS dict:

| job_id  | scraped.location             | Passes?         |
| ------- | ---------------------------- | --------------- |
| J685745 | "Runcorn"                    | ✓ only one     |
| J849031 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |
| J442509 | "Crewe"                      | ✗ not in TOWNS |
| J576140 | "2 Locations"                | ✗              |
| J858474 | "Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"   | ✗              |
| J355784 | "Bangor Bus Depot"           | ✗              |
| J936283 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |

Root causes:

- **Country suffix**: `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` — need to strip `, United Kingdom`
- **Unknown cities**: `"Crewe"`, `"Knutsford"` — present in profile `includes`, missing from TOWNS
- **Placeholders**: `"2 Locations"`, `"10 Locations"` — must fall back to `structured_job.locations`
- **Addresses**: `"Bangor Bus Depot"`, `"Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"` — need city extraction
- **Empty location**: 420 jobs have no location — all silently lost

---

### 3. `scraped.title` contains abbreviations and truncations

The scraper frequently stores garbage instead of the real title:

| scraped.title | structured_job / title_tag                   |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| "HC engineer" | "HV Commissioning Engineer"                  |
| "MD engineer" | "Mechanical Design Engineer"                 |
| "SC systems"  | "Software & Control Systems Engineers"       |
| "SM manager"  | "Senior Marketing Manager - Financial Lines" |

`match_jobs` compares against `row["title"]` which comes from `scraped.title`. The real title is in `page.title_tag` or `page.structured_job.title` — matching must use those.

---

### 4. `matched_titles` — substring instead of word-by-word matching

```python
# v1: substring containment
return [t for t in titles if t in job_title]
```

Spec requires: *"every word of the profile title appears in the job's real title in any order, ignoring case, punctuation & a trailing plural s"*.

What breaks with substring:

- `"cnc miller" in "CNC Miller"` → `False` (case-sensitive)
- `"Quality Engineer" in "Quality and Warranty Engineer"` → `False` (words not adjacent)
- `"Controls Engineer" in "Senior Controls Engineer"` → `True` — works by coincidence

From labelled data: job `J602066` has title `"Quality and Warranty Engineer"` and should match profile title `"Quality Engineer"` (both words present), but substring check returns `False`.

---

### 5. Company matching — exact equality against `scraped.company` only

```python
# v1
if row["company"] not in companies:  # exact string from scraped.company
    reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
```

Problems:

- `scraped.company` often contains a different company than what's on the page (e.g. `scraped="Viaduct Thornbury Systems"` vs `structured_job.company="Delta North Granary"`)
- Profile names include legal suffixes (`Ltd`, `ENGINEERING LTD`, `The Group`, `Holdings`, `UK`) that may differ from scraped data — spec requires fuzzy matching ignoring those suffixes

From labelled data: `J809819` — `scraped.company = "Cobalt Zephyr Holdings"`, profile contains `"Cobalt Zephyr"` → should match, but doesn't due to the `Holdings` suffix.

Spec also requires checking the company name **across the whole page** (title_tag, h1, URL, visible_text, structured_job) — pipeline only looks at `scraped.company`.

---

### 6. Remote location type not implemented

Profile contains:

```json
{"name": "Remote (UK)", "type": "remote", "includes": ["Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"]}
```

`towns_covered()` returns `{"Remote (UK)", "Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"}`, but `row["town"]` comes from the TOWNS dict which contains none of these values. Remote jobs never match.

Spec: remote = jobs where the employer explicitly states remote/home-based in that country — must check `visible_text` and `structured_job.locations`.

---

### 7. `structured_job.locations` is never used

135 jobs have `structured_job.locations` — a list of strings like `["Birmingham, GB"]`, `["manchester, Lancashire, United Kingdom"]`, `["United Kingdom", "Remote"]`. This is the most reliable location source, but the pipeline ignores it entirely.

---

### 8. `normalise_job_rows` — silent error swallowing

```python
try:
    scraped = raw["scraped"]
    rows.append({...})
except Exception:
    pass  # row silently lost — no rejection reason, no SLI entry
```

---

### 9. `parse_salary` crashes on real data

Values in the feed: `"£50K per Annum"`, `"1K - 3K per Annum"`, `"$2 per Annum"` — all cause `ValueError` inside `int(...)`. Not critical (only 12 jobs have salary), but combined with the `except Exception: pass` above, rows are silently lost.

---

### 10. Dedup by `title|company` instead of `job_id`

[drop_duplicate_jobs.py:18](v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/drop_duplicate_jobs.py#L18): key `f"{row['title']}|{row['company']}"`.

Two different jobs at the same company with the same title in different cities will be incorrectly merged. The correct key is `job_id`.

## Data Analysis — data/ (excluding golden)

### 1. jobs_raw.jsonl — 1,529 jobs

HTTP status breakdown:

| Status        | Count | %     |
| ------------- | ----- | ----- |
| 200 OK        | 868   | 56.8% |
| 403 Forbidden | 455   | 29.8% |
| 410 Gone      | 129   | 8.4%  |
| 404 Not Found | 46    | 3.0%  |
| Other / empty | 31    | 2.0%  |

43% of jobs are inaccessible. Of those, 11.4% are dead links (404/410) that should be filtered.

Field fill rates:

| Field               | Filled                       |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| scraped.title       | 100%                         |
| scraped.company     | 100%                         |
| scraped.location    | 72.5% (420 missing)          |
| scraped.salary      | 0.8% (12 of 1,529)           |
| page.title_tag      | 39.8%                        |
| page.meta           | 38.8%                        |
| page.structured_job | 27.1%                        |
| page.h1             | 16.0%                        |
| page.visible_text   | 0% (empty in entire dataset) |

**Critical finding:** `visible_text` is completely empty across the whole dataset. The company-matching rule from OUTPUT_FORMAT.json (search across page body text) cannot be applied — there is no data to search.

### 2. Location signals

- Unique location strings: 340
- 212 jobs have `"2 Locations"`, 46 have `"3 Locations"`, etc. — these are not parsed
- Top real locations: London (37), Derby (32), Bristol (24), Glasgow (17)
- Matches against profile cities (naive search): 164 / 1,529 (10.7%)

### 3. Title signals (word-level matching)

- Unique job titles: 1,348
- Matches against profile (all words present in title): 118 / 1,529 (7.7%)
- Top matched profile titles: Controls Engineer (24), Electrical Engineer (12), Design Engineer (10), Operations Manager (9), Maintenance Technician (9)

### 4. Company signals

- Profile companies: 408 (199 with industry specified)
- Company matches (normalised): 1,049 / 1,529 (68.6%)
- High match rate because the entire feed appears to have been generated from the same company list.

### 5. Signal intersection

| Condition                              | Jobs          |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Company only                           | 1,049 (68.6%) |
| Title only                             | 118 (7.7%)    |
| Location only                          | 164 (10.7%)   |
| All three (company + title + location) | 35 (2.3%)     |

### 6. labelled_sample.jsonl — 60 labelled jobs

- yes (match): 11 (18.3%)
- no: 49 (81.7%)

All 60 job_ids are present in jobs_raw.jsonl. Of the 11 positives, only 9 have `matched_company` / `matched_location` / `matched_job_title` filled; 2 have those fields empty despite `decision=yes` — an annotation anomaly.

---

## Data investigation: run `20261020T153054` vs `profile_a` inputs

### Pipeline funnel — where jobs are lost

```
load_job_feed        1529  →  pass: 1529 (100%)
drop_duplicates      1517  →  pass: 1445 (95.3%)  | rejected: 72 DUPLICATE
resolve_job_town     1445  →  pass:     6 (0.4%)  | rejected: 1439 UNKNOWN_LOCATION  ← BOTTLENECK
match_jobs              6  →  pass:     2 (33.3%) | rejected: 3 COMPANY_NOT_LISTED, 1 NO_TITLE_MATCH
OUTPUT                  2 jobs
```

### Signal correlation with the dataset

| Dimension                                           | Matches           | % of 1,529 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------- |
| Company (exact match)                               | **1,021**   | 66.8%      |
| Location (token match against towns)                | **136**     | 8.9%       |
| Title (word-match against profile)                  | ~**160**    | ~10.5%     |
| **Triple intersection (manual analysis)**     | **56**      | 3.7%       |
| Of which false-geo (Liverpool NSW, Warrington PA…) | −6               |            |
| **Real UK jobs that should match**            | **~48–50** |            |
| **Worker found**                              | **2**       | 0.13%      |

### Root cause: `resolve_job_town` only handles bare-city lookup

Location format breakdown in the dataset:

| Format                           | Count       | Worker handling              |
| -------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `"City, United Kingdom"`       | 567 (37%)   | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |
| Bare city (1–2 words)           | 459 (30%)   | ✅ only if in hardcoded dict |
| Empty string                     | 420 (27.5%) | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |
| `"Hybrid - 2 days Warrington"` | 1 (0.1%)    | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |
| US/AU false positives            | 15 (1%)     | needs country filter         |

Of the 567 jobs with `"City, United Kingdom"` format — **80 have a city from the profile** (Manchester, Birmingham, Liverpool, etc.) and all are lost because the resolver cannot strip the `, United Kingdom` suffix.

### The 6 jobs that passed the resolver

Only jobs with a **bare city name** (`Wrexham`, `Chester`, `Runcorn`) hit the hardcoded TOWNS dict. Of those:

- **2 passed** (Inkwell Copperleaf Group — present in companies list, Wrexham → North Wales)
- **3 rejected** at COMPANY_NOT_LISTED (`Mersey Ironbridge`, `Moorside Millrace` — not in the list)
- **1 rejected** at NO_TITLE_MATCH (`Software Engineer III, Digital Pathology…` — `systems engineer` is too weak a match)

### Top missed patterns (54 missed of 56)

53 of 54 are blocked at `resolve_job_town`. Main patterns:

- `"Bolton, GB"` — 5 Controls Engineer jobs @ Aire Calder / Aire Northwind / Ancoats Castlefield
- `"Manchester, United Kingdom"` — 4 jobs
- `"Liverpool, United Kingdom"` — 4 jobs
- `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` — 6 jobs
- `"Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"` — 3 jobs at Lowther Brindley
- `"Wolverhampton, United Kingdom"` — 2 jobs

### Conclusion

The worker **works** — architecture and contracts are correct. But `resolve_job_town` is an intentionally broken module (noted in CLAUDE.md): it uses exact-match against a tiny hardcoded dict, whereas the real requirement is parsing multi-format location strings. Fixing this module alone would raise output from 2 to ~48 jobs (~24×).

## `normalise_job_rows` — 8 тестов

| Тест                                                   | Причина падения                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `test_parse_salary_k_suffix`                             | `parse_salary("£50K per Annum")` → `int("50K per Annum")` → `ValueError`                                        |
| `test_parse_salary_range_with_k`                         | `parse_salary("1K - 3K per Annum")` → та же ошибка                                                          |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[£31K per Annum]`   | K-суффикс, другая сумма                                                                                |

| `test_normalise_missing_scraped_has_sli_entry`           | `except Exception: pass` — строка теряется молча, в SLI-лог ничего не попадает |

**Корень:** `parse_salary` делает `int(str(value).replace("£","").replace(",",""))` — не обрабатывает суффиксы, диапазоны и чужие символы.

---

## `drop_duplicate_jobs` — 1 тест

import pytest

def test_resolve_known_town(ctx):
    rows = [make_row(location="Warrington")]
    result = resolve_job_town.main(ctx, rows)
    assert len(result.data) == 1
    row = result.data[0]
    assert row["town"] == "Warrington"
    assert row["region"] == "North West England"
    assert row["country"] == "United Kingdom"
    assert row["used_llm"] is False


def test_resolve_case_insensitive(ctx):
    rows = [make_row(location="warrington")]
    result = resolve_job_town.main(ctx, rows)
    assert len(result.data) == 1
    assert result.data[0]["town"] == "Warrington"


def test_resolve_unknown_location_rejected(ctx):
    rows = [make_row(location="Unknown City XYZ")]
    result = resolve_job_town.main(ctx, rows)
    assert len(result.data) == 0


def test_resolve_sli_marks_unknown_location(ctx, tmp_path):
    rows = [make_row(location="Unknown City XYZ")]
    resolve_job_town.main(ctx, rows)
    sli = read_sli(tmp_path)
    assert any(e.get(META_REJECTION_REASON) == "UNKNOWN_LOCATION" for e in sli)

    rows = [make_row(location="")]
    result = resolve_job_town.main(ctx, rows)
    assert len(result.data) == 0

    """Runcorn is in TOWNS dict — resolves successfully."""
    rows = [make_row(location="Runcorn")]

    assert len(result.data) == 1
    assert result.data[0]["town"] == "Runcorn"

    assert len(result.data) == 1
    assert result.data[0]["town"] == "Wrexham"
    assert result.data[0]["region"] == "Wales"

    """Known towns pass; unknown are rejected. Only known rows come back."""
    rows = [
        make_row(job_id="J001", location="Warrington"),
        make_row(job_id="J002", location="Unknown City XYZ"),
        make_row(job_id="J003", location="Liverpool"),

    assert "Controls Engineer" in result

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from v1.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import run_pipeline
from v1.workers.job_matcher import handler

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
LABELLED = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "labelled_sample.jsonl"
JOBS_RAW = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "jobs_raw.jsonl"
SEARCH_INPUTS = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "user_search_inputs"


@pytest.fixture
def labelled_data():
    if not LABELLED.exists():
        pytest.skip("data/labelled_sample.jsonl not present")
    return [json.loads(line) for line in LABELLED.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]


@pytest.fixture
def raw_jobs():
    if not JOBS_RAW.exists():
        pytest.skip("data/jobs_raw.jsonl not present")
    result = {}
    with JOBS_RAW.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            if line.strip():
                row = json.loads(line)
                result[row["job_id"]] = row
    return result


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Labelled sample shape / content sanity checks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_labelled_sample_has_expected_shape(labelled_data):
    """Sanity check: 60 rows, each with decision/reason/matched_* fields."""
    assert len(labelled_data) == 60
    for row in labelled_data:
        assert "job_id" in row
        assert row["decision"] in ("yes", "no")
        assert "reason" in row


def test_labelled_yes_jobs_count(labelled_data):
    yes = [r for r in labelled_data if r["decision"] == "yes"]
    assert len(yes) == 11


def test_labelled_no_jobs_include_dead_links(labelled_data, raw_jobs):
    """8 of the 'no' labels are 404/410 jobs — documents the dead-link bug scope."""
    dead_nos = [
        label
        for label in labelled_data
        if label["decision"] == "no"
        and raw_jobs.get(label["job_id"], {}).get("page", {}).get("http_status") in (404, 410)
    ]
    assert len(dead_nos) >= 8


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Full pipeline integration: 1529-job feed against profile_a
# These numbers come from run 20261020T153054 and must stay stable.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _run_full_pipeline(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> set[str]:
    """Helper: run v1 on jobs_raw.jsonl vs profile_a, return matched job_id set."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    if not JOBS_RAW.exists() or not SEARCH_INPUTS.exists():
        pytest.skip("data/ files not present")
    outputs = run_pipeline(
        handler.STAGE_GRAPH,
        handler.INPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA,
        handler.OUTPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA,
        handler.HANDLER_NAME,
        JOBS_RAW,
        SEARCH_INPUTS,
    )
    matched: set[str] = set()
    for path in outputs:
        for line in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                matched.add(json.loads(line)["job_id"])
    return matched


def test_v1_full_pipeline_output_count(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """v1 outputs exactly 2 matched jobs on the full 1529-job feed (run 20261020T153054 baseline)."""
    matched = _run_full_pipeline(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    assert len(matched) == 2


def test_v1_full_pipeline_matches_correct_jobs(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """The 2 matched jobs are J678841 and J948846 (Inkwell Copperleaf Group, Wrexham)."""
    matched = _run_full_pipeline(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    assert matched == {"J678841", "J948846"}


def test_v1_full_pipeline_j685745_not_matched(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """J685745 (Runcorn, Driftwood Copperleaf) passes resolve_job_town but fails NO_TITLE_MATCH.
    Title is 'Software Engineer III, Digital Pathology...' — no profile title is a substring."""
    matched = _run_full_pipeline(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    assert "J685745" not in matched


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pipeline on the 60 labelled jobs — recall measurement
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_v1_pipeline_on_labelled_subset(tmp_path, monkeypatch, labelled_data, raw_jobs):
    """Run v1 pipeline on the 60 labelled jobs; measure recall against YES decisions.

    v1 is expected to match 0/11 YES jobs due to combined location + title bugs.
    This test documents the baseline; changing the assertion requires a real improvement.
    """
    monkeypatch.setenv("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    if not SEARCH_INPUTS.exists():
        pytest.skip("data/ files not present")
    labelled_ids = {r["job_id"] for r in labelled_data}
    subset = [raw_jobs[jid] for jid in labelled_ids if jid in raw_jobs]
    jobs_file = tmp_path / "labelled_jobs.jsonl"
    jobs_file.write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(j) for j in subset) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    outputs = run_pipeline(
        handler.STAGE_GRAPH,
        handler.INPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA,
        handler.OUTPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA,
        handler.HANDLER_NAME,
        jobs_file,
        SEARCH_INPUTS,
    )
    matched_ids: set[str] = set()
    for path in outputs:
        for line in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                matched_ids.add(json.loads(line)["job_id"])
    yes_ids = {r["job_id"] for r in labelled_data if r["decision"] == "yes"}
    recall = len(yes_ids & matched_ids) / len(yes_ids) if yes_ids else 0.0
    print(f"\nv1 recall on YES labelled jobs: {recall:.0%} ({len(yes_ids & matched_ids)}/{len(yes_ids)})")
    assert recall >= 0.0


@pytest.mark.xfail(
    strict=True,
    reason=(
        "v1 bugs: all 11 YES jobs dropped — resolve_job_town rejects 10 on UNKNOWN_LOCATION, "
        "1 (J685745) on NO_TITLE_MATCH — recall is 0%"
    ),
)
def test_v1_pipeline_recall_above_50_percent(tmp_path, monkeypatch, labelled_data, raw_jobs):
    """Documents: v1 fails to reach even 50% recall on labelled YES jobs."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    if not SEARCH_INPUTS.exists():
        pytest.skip("data/ files not present")
    labelled_ids = {r["job_id"] for r in labelled_data}
    subset = [raw_jobs[jid] for jid in labelled_ids if jid in raw_jobs]
    jobs_file = tmp_path / "labelled_jobs.jsonl"
    jobs_file.write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(j) for j in subset) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    outputs = run_pipeline(
        handler.STAGE_GRAPH,
        handler.INPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA,
        handler.OUTPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA,
        handler.HANDLER_NAME,
        jobs_file,
        SEARCH_INPUTS,
    )
    matched_ids: set[str] = set()
    for path in outputs:
        for line in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                matched_ids.add(json.loads(line)["job_id"])
    yes_ids = {r["job_id"] for r in labelled_data if r["decision"] == "yes"}
    recall = len(yes_ids & matched_ids) / len(yes_ids)
    assert recall >= 0.50

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from tests.v1.helpers import make_row
from v1.workers.job_matcher.modules import portal_matches_output

REQUIRED_FIELDS = {
    "job_id", "profile_id", "matched_company",
    "matched_job_title", "matched_location", "reason", "used_llm",
}


def make_matched_row(**kwargs) -> dict:
    """Normalised row with all match fields populated."""
    return make_row(
        matched_company="Acme Corp",
        matched_job_title=["Controls Engineer"],
        matched_location=["Warrington"],
        reason="Controls Engineer at Acme Corp, in Warrington",
        used_llm=False,
        **kwargs,
    )


def test_portal_output_file_created(ctx, profile, tmp_path):
    ctx["profile"] = profile
    ctx["output_prefix"] = "profile_test"
    result = portal_matches_output.main(ctx, [make_matched_row()])
    assert Path(result.artifacts["output_path"]).exists()


def test_portal_output_file_name(ctx, profile, tmp_path):
    ctx["profile"] = profile
    ctx["output_prefix"] = "profile_test"
    result = portal_matches_output.main(ctx, [make_matched_row()])
    assert Path(result.artifacts["output_path"]).name == "profile_test_matched.jsonl"


def test_portal_output_has_required_fields(ctx, profile, tmp_path):
    ctx["profile"] = profile
    ctx["output_prefix"] = "profile_test"
    result = portal_matches_output.main(ctx, [make_matched_row()])
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in Path(result.artifacts["output_path"]).read_text().splitlines()]

## Входные данные

Два источника, оба читаются при старте:

**1. Лента вакансий** — `data/jobs_raw.jsonl`, ~1529 строк. Каждая строка:

```json
{
  "job_id": "J123456",
  "scraped": { "title": "...", "company": "...", "location": "...", "salary": "..." },
  "source_url": "...",
  "page": {
    "http_status": 200,
    "title_tag": "...", "h1": "...", "meta": {}, "visible_text": "",
    "structured_job": { "title": "...", "company": "...", "locations": ["..."] }
  }
}
```

**2. Профиль рекрутера** — `data/user_search_inputs/profile_a/`, три файла:

```
company_searches.json     → список компаний с отраслью
job_title_searches.json   → список тайтлов
location_searches.json    → список локаций с типом и includes
```

`load_search_inputs()` сливает их в один dict `context["profile"]`.

---

## Как работает матчинг (pipeline funnel)

```
load_job_feed       читает JSONL построчно
      ↓
normalise_job_rows  берёт scraped.{title,company,location,salary} → row["title"] и т.д.
      ↓
drop_duplicate_jobs dedup по ключу title|company (баг — должен быть job_id)
      ↓
resolve_job_town    lookup_town(row["location"]) → row["town"]
                    exact-match против маленького TOWNS dict
                    ❌ 99.6% вакансий отсеивается здесь (UNKNOWN_LOCATION)
      ↓
match_jobs          три проверки подряд:
  1. company:   row["company"] in {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}
  2. title:     any(t in row["title"] for t in profile["titles"])   ← substring, case-sensitive
  3. location:  row["town"] in towns_covered(loc) for any loc
```

Реальный funnel на полной ленте (run `20261020T153054`):

| Модуль | На входе | Прошло |
|--------|----------|--------|
| load_job_feed | — | 1 529 |
| drop_duplicates | 1 529 | 1 445 |
| resolve_job_town | 1 445 | **6** |
| match_jobs | 6 | **2** |

---

## Выходные данные

Файл `runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl` — одна JSON-строка на вакансию:

```json
{
  "job_id": "J678841",
  "profile_id": "a",
  "matched_company": "Inkwell Copperleaf Group",
  "matched_job_title": ["Controls Engineer"],
  "matched_location": ["Wrexham"],
  "reason": "Controls Engineer at Inkwell Copperleaf Group, in Wrexham",
  "used_llm": false
}
```

Плюс два диагностических файла:
- `sli_events.jsonl` — одна запись на строку на модуль (outcome + rejection_reason)
- `llm_calls.jsonl` — все LLM-вызовы (в v1 пустой, LLM не используется)
